analysis:
Reviewed all three primary analyses and independently checked the available replayed patches/source. ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift:17-44 records request receipt and replaces the separate authorization predicate with ServingReadiness: only blocked connections with advertised models accumulate refusal time; authorized resets retries, while pending/unconfirmed clears the timer. UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift:18-38 retains the 15-minute threshold, jitter, idle requirement and exponential backoff. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift:155-169 adds an internal receive timestamp; Service/DaemonStateFile.swift:338-345 persists an optional last-request timestamp, not request content or credentials.
No concrete security regression is established by the visible changes. Request observation is not visibly a serving grant, and no supplied change demonstrates an encryption fallback, attestation bypass, billing change, cache-isolation weakening (T-041), or expansion of privileged-helper authority. Relevant boundaries are TB-002/TB-011 and T-052/T-053/T-057, with A-016 authorization and A-018 availability.
Material questions remain because replay is incomplete (13 units omitted), including the full ServingReadiness implementation and Serve.swift request/control dispatch. Verify that the reported 60-second refusal lifetime does not indefinitely suppress the 15-minute recovery threshold when a genuinely stranded connection receives no repeated status; the coordinator's repeat-status contract is not established here. Confirm that lastRequestAt resets on each socket, locally captured receive times preserve ordering, and receipt before admission remains routing evidence only: it must not override revocation, expiry or final admission checks. Also confirm planned reconnect closes admission without disrupting cancellation or add-on holds. The local analyses raise these questions but do not prove vulnerabilities; missing implementations and external contracts require targeted further review, not findings.
